qwen.ref_text: On the battlefield, four players with monster-like strength appeared. Each of the players had already destroyed their colonies. These players were so equally strong, they created a four-way deadlock.

lines: Lecture one. Nature-inspired computing. This is how evolution became a way of solving problems.
For billions of years, nature has been solving hard problems. So we copy it. In evolution, the fitter ones survive, and they breed.
Evolution: the fitter ones survive and breed.
In the brain, the connections that prove useful grow stronger.
Brains: useful connections get stronger.
In an ant colony, the shorter trail collects more scent.
Ants: short trails get more scent.
In none of these is anyone in charge. Today, we copy evolution.
No one is in charge. Today: evolution.
Here is the goal: turn the letters Q Z T into the word C A T. The score is how many letters are right.
Goal: turn QZT into CAT. Score = letters right.
Change one letter at random. If it is not worse, keep it.
Change one letter at random. Not worse? Keep it.
If it is worse, throw the change away.
Worse? Throw it away.
Small steps add up. That is called cumulative selection.
Progress adds up. That is cumulative selection.
Both methods get the same target, and the same number of tries.
Same target. Same number of tries.
The monkey starts from scratch every single time.
The monkey starts from scratch every time.
Keep-if-better locks in each correct letter as it goes.
Keep-if-better locks in each correct letter.
The monkey's best result is still only six letters out of twenty-eight.
The monkey's best is still 6 of 28.
There are twenty-seven choices for each of twenty-eight places. Multiply twenty-seven, again and again.
27 choices for each of 28 places: 27 × 27 × … × 27.
On average the monkey needs about ten to the forty tries. The keeper needs about three thousand.
Monkey: 1.2 × 10⁴⁰ tries on average. Keeper: 3,037.
Picture a landscape, where height means how good a solution is.
A landscape: height is how good.
One climber keeps a step only if it is not worse.
One climber keeps a step if it is not worse.
So it gets stuck on the first hill it finds.
Stuck on the first hill.
Now twenty climbers spread out, and compete.
Twenty climbers spread out and compete.
Each square is one run. In two hundred runs, one climber reaches the top forty-two times, and twenty climbers do it a hundred and sixty-seven times.
Each square is one run. More climbers find the top.
Here are four parents, with fitness nine, six, three and one.
Four parents with fitness 9, 6, 3 and 1.
Fitter parents are more likely to be picked. We pick twenty times.
Fitter parents are likelier to be picked, 20 times.
If we only pick the best, everyone becomes a copy of it.
Only the best? Everyone becomes a copy.
If everyone has equal chances, nothing pushes us towards better.
Equal chances? Nothing pushes towards better.
The answer is a weak bias. Fitter is likelier, but nobody is shut out.
Weak bias: fitter is likelier, nobody is shut out.
Mutation copies a parent, and changes one gene.
Mutation: copy a parent, change one gene.
Recombination mixes pieces of two parents.
Recombination: mix pieces of two parents.
Mutation is needed. Recombination often helps.
Mutation is needed. Recombination often helps.
First, score every dot. Its height is its fitness.
Score every dot: height is fitness.
Next, pick parents. The fitter the dot, the likelier it is chosen.
Pick parents: the fitter, the likelier.
Optionally, mix two parents together.
Optional: mix two parents.
Then mutate. Nudge each child a little.
Mutate: nudge each child a little.
The children become the new population.
The children become the new population.
Repeat, and the dots climb towards the star.
Repeat: the dots climb towards the star.
Here the score is the number of green boxes. An evolutionary algorithm needs only a score.
Score = green boxes. An EA only needs a score.
Planning, design, simulation, identification, control and classification all fit. They share one requirement: you can score it.
Six areas, one requirement: you can score it.
So, anything you can score, you can evolve.
Anything you can score, you can evolve.
Copy nature, and keep what works.
Evolution needs a population, selection, mutation and recombination.
If you can score it, you can evolve it.
